points.description: States that a binary search tree is a binary tree (each node has at most two children, left and right). Merely saying 'a tree' without the binary/two-children restriction earns no marks.

levels.says: Says it is a tree with nodes but does not clearly state the at-most-two-children (binary) property.

points.description: States the ordering property: for any node, values in/at the left child (left subtree) are smaller than the node's value. Equivalent wording such as 'less than or equal' is acceptable.

States that values in/at the right child (right subtree) are larger than the node's value (greater than or equal acceptable). Must be the correct direction; reversed left/right does not earn the mark.

States that the ordering property holds for every node in the tree (applied recursively/for all nodes, so left < parent < right at each node). Accept mention that it enables efficient searching/in-order traversal gives sorted order as supporting evidence of this.

rubric.notes: Full marks: a binary tree where, for every node, left child/subtree is smaller and right child/subtree is larger than the node. Part marks for giving only one side of the ordering or a vague 'ordered tree'. No marks for descriptions of unrelated structures or reversed ordering.
